The name Masheer is stated to be derived from the Arabic word 'maashi', which means 'stones'. The town was significant due to its fertile land and strategic location, making it a target for various Islamic dynasties throughout history.

Al-Idrisi's 'Nuzhat al-Mushtaq fi Ikhtiraq al-Afak' (The Pleasurable Journey to the Ends of the Earth), written around 1154 CE. This geographical work describes Masheer as a city near the Mediterranean coast, belonging to the Zirid Dynasty. The name Masheer is mentioned as derived from the Arabic word 'maashi', which means 'horses'. The city was significant due to its agricultural wealth, especially its production of horses and grapes.
